key_findings: 18 kestrel crons currently running: 3 self-healing (freshness-watchdog 60s, post-ingest-scorer 60s, compound-state 5min), rest are RSS/huntsystems legacy
Freshness watchdog checks 222 tracked sources every 60s against expected cadence, auto-quarantines at 10 consecutive stale cycles
Flocks not needed because each cron writes to its own DuckDB partition or state file, not shared resources
Systemd WatchdogSec dead-letter: cron jobs don't easy restart via systemd; a separate watchdog cron that checks stale timestamps and re-spawns is more reliable
State file (cycle-state/current.json) is 15KB with full agent/source/budget/alerts state — any agent can read it in one shot, saved ~50K tokens per session
Self-healing paired crons (watchdog + recovery) catch more failure modes than monolithic orchestrator because each has a single responsibility
222 sources tracked means ~200 are auto-detected Telegram @handles that need content-based merge/dedup with known channels
0 source_agreement rows means cross-source bucketing hasn't triggered — needs ~15min of multiple sources hitting same asset to populate
All 4434 events have uniform edge_score (0.149) because source detection fails for 3667/4434 — no baseline differentiation without proper source_id
uncertainties: Whether content-based source detection from Telegram message bodies will correctly resolve 3667 unknown-telegram-export events
Whether cross-source agreement (source_agreement table) actually fires — needs binned events from 2+ sources hitting same asset in 15-min window
Whether budget guard ($2 pause) is wired to actually stop crons vs just flagging alerts
Whether 222 tracked sources includes actual duplicate entries from auto-detected @handle variants
research_gaps: Content-based source detection: @handle extraction from message bodies works (catches @GemHunterrs, @disclosetv) but 3667/4434 still unknown — need HTML title tag parser and channel-level classification
Systemd timer replacement: cron jobs lack systemd-style restart limits and WatchdogSec — recovery relies on next cron cycle catching failure
Exponential backoff: no retry delay for failed jobs — they just run again on next schedule
Flocks not tested: no lock enforcement between duplicate cron instances (RSS pollers could double-fire)
Orchestrator vs standalone: no master state machine to prevent cascading failures when DuckDB goes offline
recommended_next_hop: Design the content-based source detection layer: parse HTML title tags from Telegram export files, extract @handle references from message bodies with dedup, merge auto-detected handles into known sources in coordination.yaml, then retroactively update the 3667 unknown events in DuckDB so scoring differentiates by baseline.
